messages.subject: multivariate statistics
messages.body_plain:
It has come to my attention that some people are interested in multivariate statistics (ordination, clustering). This is a short list of literature I was able to browse through (or read). For us beginners, I would recommend Kindt & Roe's Tree diversity analysis (available on-line for free) and for a bit more advanced users of R, User manual of PRIMER package (Change in marine communities: An approach to statistical analysis and interpretation) by Clarke & Warwick. The former gives a detailed procedure of coding, as well as providing a GUI to BiodiversityR package (a wrapper for package vegan) and the latter gives a better theoretical background to the methods (see also Statistical ecology in practice by Waite). There is also Tabachnik's Using multivariate statistics and I'm sure many more books and others texts (please post titles and your comments on the book if you know of any). For people with specific questions about ecology and R are able to post on r-sig-ecology mailing list (as well as here, of course!). I would be very interested in hearing your data analysis in ecology, as I'm currently analyzing using ordination and clustering method myself.

Cheers,
Roman

messages.body_plain:
Razmišljanje po sestanku, delavnici:

Mislim, da je bila delavnica neproduktivna, saj je nemogoče pripraviti
predavanje, ki bo hkrati zanimivo in uporabno za začetnike in izkušene
uporabnike. Sam sem nekje vmes.

Začetniki so obupali po nekaj minutah, ko je bila količina informacij
in podrobnosti prevelika, da bi se jim sploh lahko zlagala v
konsistentno celoto, izkušeni uporabniki pa so se v teh minutah še
dolgočasili, kasneje pa dobili tu in tam kak uporaben namig.

Začetniki seveda nimajo težav s posameznimi podrobnostmi delovanja R,
saj imajo še splošno težavo, kako se sploh lotiti R-ja in preklopiti
iz logike uporabe gumbov in menijev na logiko uporabe napisanih
ukazov.

Napredni uporabniki pa domnevno uporabljajo R za obdelavo svojih
podatkov, kjer se rutine ponavljajo, in ko so enkrat dojeli, kako
stvar deluje, ne potrebujejo več različnih variant, kako bi isto
težavo lahko rešili, ampak predvsem pomoč pri konkretnih ovirah, na
katere naletijo. Šele v tej fazi se pojavijo zelo konkretna vprašanja,
ki pa se spet od uporabnika do uporabnika razlikujejo in za reševanje
takih vprašanj je vsekakor bolj primerno mesto forum, ki dejansko
uspešno deluje.

Torej mislim, da bi bilo nujno za prihodnje delavnice jasno definirati
ciljno publiko in tej publiki prilagoditi teorijo in prakso (slednja
je za začetnike še posebej nujna). In za dosego uspešnega napredka
začetniških uporabnikov bi bilo še kako koristno tudi razdeljevanje
"domačih nalog", pa čeprav zveni malo hecno, ampak ko bi prejeto
znanje nekdo preizkusil na lastnih vhodnih podatkih, ki jih približno
razume in ve, kaj od njih pričakuje, bi šele absolviral neko poglavje
in razvil vprašanja ter bil pripravljen na nadgradnjo.

Mimogrede, ker sem manjkal na prvem sestanku, le vprašanje:
se je od članov interesne skupine sploh zbralo osnovne podatke, v
kateri fazi uporabe R je kdo, za kaj bi ga rad uporabljal, kakšni so
njegovi vhodni podatki, koliko je domač z ukaznim upravljanjem s
programi... temu bi se potem lahko prilagodilo vsebino nadaljnjih
sestankov.

Aja, da ne bo kdo mislil, da poskušam delovati destruktivno!
Nasprotno, zelo sem navdušen nad idejo od samega začetka in ravno zato
želim, da bi bila izpeljava bolj učinkovita.
N

Zdravo vsem,

Nejc, hvala za te misli. Že po sami delavnici nas je kar nekaj ostalo
in smo diskutirali prav o problemih, ki si jih omenil. No, to
Rkoholično gibanje je še čisto v povojih in ni bilo za pričakovati, da
bo zadeva šla skozi brez porodnih krčev.

Verjetno bi bilo res smiselno, vsaj na začetku, narediti dve "ravni"
delavnic (začetniki/napredni uporabniki). Težava je, da je (vsaj če
sodimo po prvi delavnici, kjer smo to vprašali) razmeroma malo
naprednih uporabnikov. To postavi dva problema: 1) malo ljudi, ki bi
lahko pripravilo vaje za začetniške delavnice, 2) malo ljudi, ki bodo
sodelovali na "naprednih" delavnicah.

Prav tako bi res morali stvari narediti interaktivne, "hands-on".
Pomeni, da lahko sodelujoči na delavnici sproti preizkušajo stvari, ki
se prezentirajo. Verjetno bi morali to postaviti kot pravilo.

Torej, z Maartenom predlagava:

- Pripraviva lahko on-line vprašalnik, kjer bo lahko vsak vpisal kako
daleč je v uporabi R-a, za kaj R uporablja / namerava uporabljati in
ali je pripravljen/a pripraviti začetniške delavnice oz. sodelovati v
naprednih delavnicah.

- Ko bomo videli, s kakšnimi resursi razpolagamo, se lahko odločimo
kako dalje. Če je dovolj ljudi, je gotovo smiselno organizirati
posebej začetniške delavnice in posebej "napredne" delavnice. Čez
nekaj časa, ko začetniki več ne bodo začetniki, delavnice spet
združimo.

- Začetniške delavnice bi začele od začetka in ljudi počasi (tudi z
domačimi nalogami) pripeljale do dovolj dobrega znanja R-a, da bodo
lahko sami nadaljevali. Te delavnice bi lahko tudi snemali in jih
objavili na Internetu (skupaj z ustrezno R kodo in podatki), da bodo
lahko sledili tudi tisti, ki se delavnic iz katerega koli razloga ne
bodo mogli udeležiti.

- Napredne delavnice se potem ne ukvarjajo z R osnovami, ampak
dejansko za prezentacijo zanimivih tehnik/R paketov/idej, metodološke
diskusije in za reševanje dejanskih problemov, s katerimi se srečujemo
pri analizi podatkov.

Kaj mislite?

Tomaž in Maarten

According to the comments I prepared a questionnaire about wishes and capacities for the Rkoholiki meetings. The idea is to get a good overview of wishes, ideas and capacities and to organize the future meetings accordingly. I hope that in this manner we'll overcome these first stumbles and make the future meetings as useful and pleasant as possible.

You can fill the questionnaire here <http://spreadsheets.google.com/viewform?formkey=dHUxcXMzYUVTZklvRm9BSTVoNlpBVEE6MA>.

Ker vem, da imamo vsi polne roke dela bom kratek. Izšla je nova verzija programa Bio7. S strani avtorjev:

The application Bio7 is an integrated development environment for ecological modelling
with a main focus on individual based modelling and spatially explicit models.

The application itself is based on an RCP-Eclipse-Environment
(Rich-Client-Platform) which offers a huge flexibility in configuration
and extensibility because of its plug-in structure and the possibility
of customization.

In še nekaj njenih zmožnosti:

- Creation and analysis of spatial explicit simulation models.
- Statistical analysis (R).
- Spatial statistics (possibility to send values from a specialized panel to R).

- Image Analysis (embedded ImageJ).
- Fast communication between R and Java (with RServe) and
   the possibilty to use R methods inside Java.

- Interpretation of Java and script creation (with BeanShell).

- Direct compilation of Java (Janino).
- Creation of methods for Java, BeanShell, Groovy and R
   (integrated editors for Java, R, BeanShell, Groovy).
- Sensitivity analysis with an embedded flowchart editor  in which

  scripts, macros and compiled code can be dragged and executed.
- Creation of 3d OpenGL (Jogl) models.
- Visualizations and simulations on an embedded 3d globe
   (World
                Wind Java SDK)

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I'd like to thank everyone for filling the questionnaire. Now, the future is not a murky dark unknown anymore, but a clear path for us to follow... :o)

First, we never discussed the official language of the mailing list, and this is something we should do. I'm currently writing in English as this forum has international membership, which will hopefully increase with other international students in the future. However, I understand that some people will not feel comfortable or confident enough to use English. My suggestion is to use both Slovenian and English interchangably, and get Google Translate <http://translate.google.com/#sl%7Cen%7C> to smooth the differences. The translations are sometimes horrible, but should get the message across. People with other suggestions are welcome to voice them.

So, I'll present a summary of the questionnaire. I'll try to keep it short, without any comments - sort of like the "results" section of a paper. I'll keep the discussion and (most of) personal comments  for  the e-mail discussion that should follow.  The entire questionnaire is still available here <http://spreadsheets.google.com/pub?key=tu1qs3aESfIoFoAI5h6ZATA&output=html> for you to look at and enjoy, but I locked it for editing.

All in all, 31 people answered the questionnaire out of the ~50 signed into the mailing list.

It seems that there are 10 people (32%) that use R (3-5 on the scale), four people (13%)  that use R every now and then (2 on the scale) and 17 (55%) that don't use R... yet.

The self-perceived knowledge (confidence in use of R) is similar… 7 people (23%) feel they know how to use R (3-5 on the scale), 14 people (45%) know the first steps (2  on the scale) and 10 people (32%) don't have a clue. Actually, some of the people in the "first steps" group are probably being too modest, so the actual base of experienced or semi-experienced users might be somewhat higher.

7 people are willing to teach beginners classes, but they are not necessary the ones that indicated they know how to use R.

19 (61%) people would like to have meetings once per month, 9  (29%) said that they'd like to meet every two weeks, one said every week, and one didn't reply to this question. Also, there was one interesting suggestion classified as "other" to have beginners meetings every two weeks as long as they are neccessary, and advanced meetings every month besides. An interesting point was made that more frequent meetings, every two weeks, would result in a more relaxed discussion as we'd get to know one another better.

All but one agree to have separate beginners/advanced user meetings. Regarding participation, 16  (52%) people would go only to beginners meetings, one person only to advanced, and 13 (42%) people to both meetings. One person didn't provide an answer.

An interesting question is the expectations - what people expect of the Rcoholic meetings. There is a large group that wants to learn R (22 people - 71%). 21 people (68%) would like to get some help with data analysis through the meetings, or have an interesting discussion about data analysis. 19  people (61%) would like an interesting discussion about R. A small, but vocal group of seven (23%) demands free coffee. There is a single voice crying out for free cocoa. A refreshment of exising R skills, helping hints from other users and info on new tools/packages were also mentioned.

Now, there is a long and diverse list of problems/techniques that people use or would like to use R for: statistical modelling - LM / GLM / GLMM and other regressions, genetics, mark-recapture, spatial analysis and simulations, making graphs, correlations, ANOVA, multivariate analyses, hypothesis testing, data processing in ethological and ecological research, testing community patterns, time series analysis, information-theoretic approach to model selection, model averaging, GOF tests for models, analysis of Q-PCR data, microarray analysis, habitat selection, spatial distribution of species with regard to habitat and interspecific interactions, modelling changes in communities caused by various environmental factors, conservation-ecological problems, classical tests, population modelling, exploratory data analysis, direct and indirect gradient analysis, minimum spanning trees, UPGMA. So, we got diversity down quite well. :) Not many people provided what sort of organisms or other topics they work on, so I'm skipping that.

There is a long list of suggestions and comments regarding the organization of meetings. I hope I'll get most of them:

1) Interactive, hands-on meetings with people working on actual data . That came up a lot.  Homework also came up several times . Go figure. :o)

2) Separated begginers/advanced meetings (there seems to be a wide agreement on that point in the questionnaire).

3) Possiblity of people to present their own problems or work through their own data.

4) More frequent meetings for beginners until they stop being beginners.

5) Posting examples and code from the presentations/exercises online after meetings.

6) Known main topics of meetings before the meetings.

7) There was also an idea about starting an internet forum, as this is more permanent than the mailing list.

8) Idea for people to bring their R books to the meetings to show them to others.

9) A "how-to" part on each meeting where people would ask how to do something, and other people would answer (presumably there is always someone that knows the answer… :o)).

10 To rotate "teachers" - an individual or a pair would prepare a topic and teach it to everyone that wishes to learn.

11) There was a long list of praise for the effort of starting the Rcoholics. Most of these should go to Maarten, who actually came up with the idea in the first place and saw it through.

So, here it is. Now, a discussion!

Tomaž

> So, I'll present a summary of the questionnaire. I'll try to keep it short,
> without any comments - sort of like the "results" section of a paper. I'll
> keep the discussion and (most of) personal comments  for  the e-mail
> discussion that should follow.  The entire questionnaire is still available

> here<http://spreadsheets.google.com/pub?key=tu1qs3aESfIoFoAI5h6ZATA&output...>for

> you to look at and enjoy, but I locked it for editing.
>
> All in all, 31 people answered the questionnaire out of the ~50 signed into
> the mailing list.
>
> It seems that there are 10 people (32%) that use R (3-5 on the scale), four
> people (13%)  that use R every now and then (2 on the scale) and 17 (55%)
> that don't use R... yet.
>

> The self-perceived knowledge (confidence in use of R) is similar... 7 people

> (23%) feel they know how to use R (3-5 on the scale), 14 people (45%) know
> the first steps (2  on the scale) and 10 people (32%) don't have a clue.
> Actually, some of the people in the "first steps" group are probably being
> too modest, so the actual base of experienced or semi-experienced users
> might be somewhat higher.
>
> 7 people are willing to teach beginners classes, but they are not necessary
> the ones that indicated they know how to use R.
>
> 19 (61%) people would like to have meetings once per month, 9  (29%) said
> that they'd like to meet every two weeks, one said every week, and one
> didn't reply to this question. Also, there was one interesting suggestion
> classified as "other" to have beginners meetings every two weeks as long as
> they are neccessary, and advanced meetings every month besides. An
> interesting point was made that more frequent meetings, every two weeks,
> would result in a more relaxed discussion as we'd get to know one another
> better.
>
> All but one agree to have separate beginners/advanced user meetings.
> Regarding participation, 16  (52%) people would go only to beginners
> meetings, one person only to advanced, and 13 (42%) people to both meetings.
> One person didn't provide an answer.
>
> An interesting question is the expectations - what people expect of the
> Rcoholic meetings. There is a large group that wants to learn R (22 people -
> 71%). 21 people (68%) would like to get some help with data analysis through
> the meetings, or have an interesting discussion about data analysis. 19
> people (61%) would like an interesting discussion about R. A small, but
> vocal group of seven (23%) demands free coffee. There is a single voice
> crying out for free cocoa. A refreshment of exising R skills, helping hints
> from other users and info on new tools/packages were also mentioned.
>
> Now, there is a long and diverse list of problems/techniques that people use
> or would like to use R for: statistical modelling - LM / GLM / GLMM and
> other regressions, genetics, mark-recapture, spatial analysis and
> simulations, making graphs, correlations, ANOVA, multivariate analyses,
> hypothesis testing, data processing in ethological and ecological research,
> testing community patterns, time series analysis, information-theoretic
> approach to model selection, model averaging, GOF tests for models, analysis
> of Q-PCR data, microarray analysis, habitat selection, spatial distribution
> of species with regard to habitat and interspecific interactions, modelling
> changes in communities caused by various environmental factors,
> conservation-ecological problems, classical tests, population modelling,
> exploratory data analysis, direct and indirect gradient analysis, minimum
> spanning trees, UPGMA. So, we got diversity down quite well. :) Not many
> people provided what sort of organisms or other topics they work on, so I'm
> skipping that.
>
> There is a long list of suggestions and comments regarding the organization
> of meetings. I hope I'll get most of them:
>
> 1) Interactive, hands-on meetings with people working on actual data . That
> came up a lot.  Homework also came up several times . Go figure. :o)
>
> 2) Separated begginers/advanced meetings (there seems to be a wide agreement
> on that point in the questionnaire).
>
> 3) Possiblity of people to present their own problems or work through their
> own data.
>
> 4) More frequent meetings for beginners until they stop being beginners.
>
> 5) Posting examples and code from the presentations/exercises online after
> meetings.
>
> 6) Known main topics of meetings before the meetings.
>
> 7) There was also an idea about starting an internet forum, as this is more
> permanent than the mailing list.
>
> 8) Idea for people to bring their R books to the meetings to show them to
> others.
>
> 9) A "how-to" part on each meeting where people would ask how to do
> something, and other people would answer (presumably there is always someone

> that knows the answer... :o)).

>
> 10 To rotate "teachers" - an individual or a pair would prepare a topic and
> teach it to everyone that wishes to learn.
>
> 11) There was a long list of praise for the effort of starting the
> Rcoholics. Most of these should go to Maarten, who actually came up with the
> idea in the first place and saw it through.
>
> So, here it is. Now, a discussion!

messages.body_plain:
Hi R koholiks,

For starters I would suggest to have our first advanced meeting on the
14th of January at 16:00h. I invited Dr. Gogala to present the package
"Seewave". This package gives you the ability to analyze acoustic data.
As Tomaz already suggested we can after that discuss about the how to
fill in the workshop for beginners. It would also be nice if some
beginners would be there to give their opinion.

Just a start for a discussion about the content of the courses and the
time table ( just to think something over during the holidays;)):
First there are several options which materials to use for the beginners
meetings: We could use the lectures of professor Blejec (off course if
that is alright with prof. Blejec), you can find parts about it on his
website "http://ablejec.nib.si/R/" or we can use the R book of M.J.
Crawley (http://www.bio.ic.ac.uk/research/mjcraw/therbook/index.htm). To
be honest I am not really familiar with prof Blejec his lecture, so I
can not tell much about it. The R book on the other hand I know more
about, this gives an introduction to the use of R with contents about
data input, manipulating dataframes, graphics, tables, mathematics,
classical tests, statistical modelling, regression, analysis of
variances, etc etc... Additionally he also provides datasets on his
website for use. If anyone else has other options please let me know.
For the advanced meetings it would be nice that everyone presents a
topic about methods they are working with ranging from simulations,
multivariate analysis, statistical modeling, genetics analyzes, etc etc.
I volunteer to gather presentations for the advanced group and schedule
them for the future meetings. So if you have any idea for a presentation
please contact me and I will put the dates in an Excel sheet online.

About the time frame: Urï¿½a suggested to have twice a month a beginners
meeting and once a month an advanced meeting. I think this is a nice
idea, as the beginners than can faster learn R and the groups can than
fuse in a later stage.
I would therefore suggest the following dates on 16h:
Beginners course:
28-1, 11-2, 25-2, 11-3, 25-3, 8-4, 22-4, etc
advanced course:
14-1,17-2, 17-3, 14-4, 13-5, etc

It would be nice if advanced users could also attend the beginners, so
they can help the beginners with R problems.

This is a kick off for this discussions, I am looking forward to your
reply and/or additions to this email.

lp,

Maarten
